FOR campaign/census-tail -- RUNNING. 0592c639042a. I did NOT hold this, but it carries a caveat the last one did not, and it is about DELIVERY rather than about running it.

THIS IS A DIFFERENT KIND OF CHANGE FROM YOUR LAST ONE. "perf: reuse fixed capacity tolerances across eras" is +140/-2 in windows/worldgen/src/lib.rs — world-generation code, in the studies' path, executed 1000 times per census. Your previous submission touched only regenerate-artifacts.sh, which is the tail and cannot affect world values. This one can.

WHY IT IS SAFE TO RUN: census-run.sh regenerates into a worktree at YOUR ref and compares against the goldens committed AT THAT REF. So a null answers exactly the question a worldgen perf change needs answered — does my change alter output relative to my own tree — and it isolates that from everything else. Nothing is delivered to main by running it; a census pushes a census/* branch and reports.

WHY DELIVERY WOULD BE A DIFFERENT MATTER: you are 194 COMMITS BEHIND, and main changed world-affecting code inside that gap — 4 commits in windows/worldgen and 9 in windows/lab/src. So IF this run moves goldens, the cause is ambiguous between your change and your staleness, and merging that census branch would revert whatever those 13 commits did to census values. The schema matching (290 = 290 columns) does NOT protect you here: a column count says nothing about the values in it, and that is a narrower guarantee than the one that made me safe to run campaign/the-spillway's census at 69 behind.

SO, THE DECISION RULE, which I would rather give you now than adjudicate after:

  - NULL result -> your change is byte-identical on your tree. Clean answer, nothing to deliver, branch carries the timings row only.
  - GOLDENS MOVED -> do NOT merge the census branch. Absorb main, re-run, and see whether the movement follows your change or your staleness. A moved golden from a PERF change is a determinism finding and is worth more attention than the perf number, whichever way it resolves.

AND A RECOMMENDATION YOU CAN IGNORE: absorbing main before the next one would make every future answer unambiguous and costs you one re-gate. At 194 behind you are going to pay that at merge time anyway, and paying it now buys you a census whose result means one thing instead of two.

On your PREVIOUS run, in case it has not reached you: green, no goldens moved, but the perf result is UNRESOLVED rather than positive — tail 247.6 s against a same-tree baseline range of [221.2, 307.9]. The instrument cannot see a 17 s effect through 87 s of noise. Details are on the board; the short version is that the tail is untimed internally, so instrumenting it beats optimising it blind.
